overal.goal: TaskStore's per-task lock (`lockTask`, built on `withFileLock`) is in memory, so it only serialises writers inside one process. A task write from another process (the CLI, `boof-runner mcp --stdio --admin`, a second server) can race the server's runner: the CLI's `modify` can read a task as `pending` while the server moves it to `running/` and deletes `pending/<id>`, and the CLI's atomic write then recreates `pending/<id>`; the reconciler prefers the newer `updated` time, so the task can look pending while it runs. Make the task lock work across processes with `withProcessLock`, as the auth store and the project store do, without making the in-process path slower than it has to be. Found in the opus review of command-template-rename-safety (M3, 2026-11-02); it existed before for every task write from another process.

rules.do: Read packages/shared/src/store.ts (lockTask, save, modify, transition), packages/shared/src/process-lock.ts and how auth-store.ts and project-store.ts use withProcessLock (lock file location, stale lock takeover by dead pid) before changing code.
Write a failing test first: two processes (child processes, not just two promises) that modify and transition the same task must not lose a write or leave a task in two status directories.
Keep the lock files out of the task directories the readers list (no stray files in tasks/pending, tasks/ongoing and so on); check that `list`, the reconciler and the plan sync ignore them.
Run `npm run typecheck && npm test` and `npm run lint` before finishing.
rules.dont: Do not change public API or MCP shapes.
Do not commit secrets, data roots or build output.

versions.version: Filed from the command-template-rename-safety review (M3, 2026-11-02); not started.

TaskStore.lockTask uses withProcessLock on tasks/.locks/<id>.lock (outside the status directories, removed on release). Measured on ext4: an empty withProcessLock about 11 ms against 0.002 ms for the in-memory lock, and about 5 ms on top of a task write (7.6 ms): a few locked operations per task run. Tests: a server-like transition loop and a modify loop in two child processes lose no write and leave one file; the lock waits for a live holder and fails with a clear error, takes over a dead one, and stays out of the status directories.

tests.strategy: A test that spawns a second node process doing transition/modify on the same task while the first does the same; assert no lost write and exactly one status directory holds the task.
